summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Ovule types: Anatropous (180° inverted, 82%), Orthotropous (0° erect), Campylotropous, Amphitropous (horseshoe body & sac), Circinotropous (360° coil). Megasporogenesis: MMC (2n) -> Meiosis -> 1 functional chalazal megaspore -> 3 free-nuclear mitoses -> 7-celled, 8-nucleate Polygonum embryo sac (3 chalazal antipodals, 1 central cell with 2 polar nuclei, 1 egg cell + 2 synergids with filiform apparatus).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
POLYGONUM-TYPE EMBRYO SAC (7-Celled, 8-Nucleate)
               
   CHALAZAL POLE ──────► 3 Antipodal Cells (n) [Ephemeral / Metabolic]
   
   CENTRAL REGION ─────► 1 Large Central Cell containing 2 Polar Nuclei (n + n)
   
   MICROPYLAR POLE ────► Egg Apparatus:
                         ├── 1 Egg Cell (n) [Female Gamete]
                         └── 2 Synergids (n) possessing Filiform Apparatus
                             (Finger-like wall invaginations guiding pollen tube)
conceptBreakdown.content:
The Gynoecium consists of one or more carpels (pistils). Each ovule (megasporangium) is attached to the placenta via a slender stalk (**Funicle**). The point of fusion between ovule body and funicle is the **Hilum**.

```
                           OVULE ANATOMICAL PARTS
                           
   Funicle (Stalk) ──► Hilum (Junction) ──► Nucellus (2n Core) ──► Integuments (Protective Coats)
                                                                            │
   Chalaza (Basal Pole) ◄───────────────────────────────────────────── Micropyle (Apical Pore)
```

### 3.1 Angiosperm Ovule Typology

```
                             OVULE STRUCTURAL TYPES
                                       │
     ┌─────────────────┬───────────────┼───────────────┬─────────────────┐
     ▼                 ▼               ▼               ▼                 ▼
 ANATROPOUS       ORTHOTROPOUS   CAMPYLOTROPOUS   AMPHITROPOUS     CIRCINOTROPOUS
 180° Inverted;   0° Completely  Curved body;     Horseshoe-shaped 360° Coiled funicle
 Micropyle near    Erect; hilum,  micropyle bent   body AND embryo  enclosing ovule
 Hilum (82%).     micropyle align at right angle.  sac (Poaceae).   (Opuntia).
```

### 3.2 Megasporogenesis & Monosporic Polygonum-Type Embryo Sac

```
                       MEGASPOROGENESIS CASCADE
                       
   Nucellar Archisporial Cell ──► Megaspore Mother Cell (MMC, 2n)
                                           │
   Meiosis I & II              ────────────┴────────────► Linear Tetrad of 4 Megaspores (n)
                                                               │
   3 Micropylar Megaspores Degenerate ◄────────────────────────┘
            │
            ▼
   1 Functional Chalazal Megaspore (n) ──► Undergoes 3 Free-Nuclear Mitotic Divisions
```

```
                 EMBRYO SAC ARCHITECTURE (MICROPYLAR TO CHALAZAL)
                 
                     [ 3 Antipodal Cells (n) ]   (Chalazal End)
                               │
               [ Large Central Cell (Polar Nuclei n + n) ]
                               │
            [ Egg Cell (n) ] + [ 2 Synergid Cells (n) ]  (Micropylar End)
                        (Filiform Apparatus)
```

- **Egg Apparatus (Micropylar Pole)**:
  - **1 Egg Cell ($n$)**: The female gamete.
  - **2 Synergids ($n$)**: Possess the **Filiform Apparatus** (finger-like wall folds secreting chemotropic attractants, e.g., LURE peptides) that guide pollen tube entry into one of the synergids.
- **Central Cell**: Largest cell containing **2 Polar Nuclei ($n+n$)**, which fuse during triple fusion to form the $3n$ PEN.
- **3 Antipodal Cells ($n$) (Chalazal Pole)**: Ephemeral, metabolically active cells providing nutritional support.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Monosporic vs Bisporic vs Tetrasporic Embryo Sacs
conceptBreakdown.title: Monosporic vs Bisporic vs Tetrasporic Embryo Sacs
conceptBreakdown.content: Monosporic (Polygonum/Oenothera): Embryo sac develops from 1 functional megaspore. Bisporic (Allium): Develops from 2 megaspore nuclei. Tetrasporic (Fritillaria/Peperomia): All 4 megaspore nuclei participate in embryo sac formation.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Obturator Structure
conceptBreakdown.title: Obturator Structure
conceptBreakdown.content: An outgrowth of the funicle or placenta called the Obturator acts as a mechanical and chemotropic guide directing the growing pollen tube into the micropyle of the ovule.
